correctness.rationale: For every SPD \(2\times2\) input, the residual is positive semidefinite rank one. Cayley–Hamilton yields \(\det(A)\|w\|_2^2/(w^{\mathsf T}Aw)\); two sign directions yield the exact Bernoulli best-of-m selection probability \(2^{-m}\); strict convexity gives the all-orientations maximum and equality cases. The uniform angular integral equals \(\sqrt{\det A}\), and AM–GM then gives the exact minimum \(m\) threshold. Standalone tests passed 33,062 exact-rational, direct matrix and angular-integral assertions. Finite tests are supplementary; infinite parameter claims have analytic proof.

value.rationale: Low-rank sketch distribution interchangeability can fail badly at small budgets because Rademacher probe directions are discrete. The complete two-dimensional minimax law identifies the worst orientation and its sharp switch at \(\kappa+1=2^m\), and gives the exact minimum number \(m\) of independent candidate matvecs needed to match the one-Gaussian expected loss uniformly in orientation. This is a natural stability and method-selection benchmark, not an arbitrary unmotivated matrix slice. It explicitly does not assert an equal-cost efficiency improvement.
